regulator: Delaware Office of the Marijuana Commissioner

data_source.name: NCS Analytics Transparency Project: Delaware (dashboard linked by the OMC)
data_source.notes: Delaware does not publish monthly sales itself; the OMC links this dashboard run by NCS Analytics, a private vendor that does not certify the data, shows only a rolling six-month window and may revise recent months. 'adult_use' and 'medical' are the dashboard's Adult Use and Medicinal retail columns as read Nov 7, 2026; the separate Wholesale column is excluded. Total = adult-use + medical. Adult-use sales began August 1, 2025.

tax_note: Adult-use marijuana carries a 15% retail marijuana tax, and buyers with a valid medical marijuana card are exempt (Delaware Division of Revenue).
summary: Delaware's adult-use sales began on August 1, 2025, at 13 former medical dispensaries that converted to serve all adults, and the market remains small. The state-linked dashboard shows $6.2 million in adult-use sales and $2.5 million in medical sales in October 2026, the highest adult-use month in its six-month window. Press reports put first-year retail sales well below the $281 million a year once projected. Few stores, higher prices than neighboring Maryland and New Jersey, and slow openings by new retail-only licensees all hold the market back. Sales should rise as the 30 retail-only licensees open.

faq.q: How much cannabis does Delaware sell a month?
faq.a: About $8.7 million in October 2026, including $6.2 million adult-use and $2.5 million medical, according to the NCS Analytics dashboard linked by the Office of the Marijuana Commissioner.

faq.q: When did adult-use cannabis sales start in Delaware?
What is the cannabis tax in Delaware?
faq.a: A 15% retail marijuana tax on adult-use purchases. Medical cardholders are exempt.
